facts.heading: Anxiety worsened in September
facts.content: Hannah feels anxious all the time, and this feeling got worse in September.
facts.evidence: I think I'm just anxious all the time and it got worse in September.

facts.heading: Promoted to deputy head role
facts.content: Hannah has taught at her school for 11 years. She was asked to step up when the deputy head left.
facts.evidence: I've taught here for 11 years and I have loved it and then they had asked me to step up and when our deputy left.

facts.heading: Fear of being inadequate
facts.content: Hannah worries that people picked the wrong person for her new role. She fears someone will notice she doesn't know what she is doing.
facts.evidence: I keep thinking they picked the wrong person, and that sooner or later someone will notice I have no idea what I'm doing.

facts.heading: Anxiety symptoms on Sunday evenings
facts.content: When the thought of inadequacy arrives, Hannah's chest tightens on Sunday evenings. She starts rehearsing Monday's staff meeting in her head.
facts.evidence: Mostly Sunday evenings, my chest goes tight and I start rehearsing Monday's staff meeting in my head.

facts.heading: Rehearsing worst-case scenarios
facts.content: Hannah rehearses every possible question someone might ask during the staff meeting. She also rehearses what others would think of her if she got it wrong.
facts.evidence: Every possible question someone might ask and what I would say, then what they would think of me if I got it wrong.

facts.heading: Fear of being seen as incompetent
facts.content: Hannah imagines people would think she is out of her depth. She fears they gave the job to a teacher who cannot read.
facts.evidence: That I'm out of my depth. That they gave the job to a nice earful teacher who can't actually read.

facts.heading: Rewrote email four times
facts.content: Last week, Hannah rewrote the same email to the governors four times. The email was about the change to the behavior policy.
facts.evidence: Last week I rewrote the same email to the governors four times.

facts.heading: Fear of Mr. Hargraves' judgment
facts.content: Hannah was afraid Mr. Hargraves, the chair of governors, would think she was stupid regarding the email.
facts.evidence: I was afraid Mr. Hargraves, the chair of governors, would think that I was stupid.

facts.heading: Mr. Hargraves has been kind
facts.content: Mr. Hargraves has been kind to Hannah. He told her in September he was delighted.
facts.evidence: He has been nothing but kind. He told me in September he was delighted.

facts.heading: Feeling like a fraud
facts.content: Hannah feels like she is lying to Mr. Hargraves about being capable. She feels like she is pretending to be someone who knows what she is doing.
facts.evidence: About being capable, as if I'm pretending.

facts.heading: Feeling like a child

facts.evidence: Most days I feel like a child wearing her mother's coat.

facts.heading: Mother was a headteacher

facts.evidence: She was a headteacher for 20 years.

facts.heading: Mother's positive reputation

facts.evidence: Everyone in the village still stops me to say what a wonderful head she was.

facts.heading: Comparing to mother's abilities
facts.content: Hannah constantly compares her own actions to her mother's. She wonders if her mother would have done everything better.
facts.evidence: Everything I do, I think, would she have done it better?

facts.heading: Mother's supportive nature

facts.evidence: She says I've always worried too much and I should stop being silly.

facts.evidence: It makes me feel like I'm making a fuss, so I don't tell her how bad it is.
